I don't have today's price move data for ConocoPhillips, so I can't tell you whether the stock went up or down. However, the recent news and oil prices point to competing pressures on the stock right now.

Oil prices have weakened this week — Brent crude dipped below $90 a barrel on hopes that the Iran conflict might end soon, with President Trump signaling a potential resolution. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, lower crude prices directly reduce the value of what they pump out of the ground. At the same time, the company just reported third-quarter earnings, which would give investors fresh data on profitability at current oil prices, and it appeared on a major investment committee's watchlist — both potential reasons for trading activity today. The spread between US oil ($99.64) and world oil prices ($107.03) remains wide, which can affect refining economics and global competitiveness.
